What happens to my Crypto exchanges (Coinbase) when I die?

Short answer: Crypto held on Coinbase forms part of your estate. Coinbase doesn't support beneficiary designations for individual accounts, so heirs need to know the account exists. The executor files an Executor Services claim with a death certificate, proof of authority such as probate or letters of administration, photo ID, and a signed letter naming the Coinbase account to receive the assets.

Key facts

  • No beneficiary designation
  • Claim via Coinbase Executor Services
  • Needs probate or equivalent authority
  • Recipient may need a Coinbase account

How do I prepare my Crypto exchanges (Coinbase) account?

  1. List every exchange account in your digital estate plan, without passwords in your will.
  2. After a death, the executor submits Coinbase's estate claim with a death certificate, probate documents and ID.
  3. The receiving person may need their own Coinbase account for the transfer.
  4. Self-custody wallets are different: without the seed phrase the funds are lost, so see crypto inheritance tools.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Official death certificate
  • Probate, Letters Testamentary, Letters of Administration, or a small estate affidavit where accepted
  • Current government photo ID of the person named in those documents
  • A signed letter directing transfer to a named Coinbase account and email

How long does it take?

Coinbase reviews claims after receiving the documents; no fixed timeframe is published.

What can't be recovered?

  • Funds in self-custody wallets if nobody has the seed phrase. No company can recover those.

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Crypto exchanges (Coinbase) when I die?

Crypto held on Coinbase forms part of your estate. Coinbase doesn't support beneficiary designations for individual accounts, so heirs need to know the account exists. The executor files an Executor Services claim with a death certificate, proof of authority such as probate or letters of administration, photo ID, and a signed letter naming the Coinbase account to receive the assets.

Can I name a beneficiary on Coinbase?

No. The assets pass according to your will or the law.

What about crypto in a hardware wallet?

No company can recover it. Your heirs need the seed phrase or an inheritance setup.

Do heirs need a Coinbase account?

Usually. The assets are transferred to a Coinbase account named in the executor's letter.

Can I name a beneficiary on Coinbase?

No. Coinbase says beneficiary designations aren't supported for individual accounts.
